slides.headline: 15 runs off six balls — Jansen's first over was chaos
slides.body: Marco Jansen's first over went off the rails — India hit 15 runs off just 6 balls. That's higher than any first over in this match by a wide margin and set the tone for a frantic start.

slides.headline: Rohit and Pant gone in the same over — India wobbled
slides.body: Maharaj struck twice in his over: Rohit was caught by Klaasen, then Pant fell to de Kock moments later. India's win chance dropped from 65% to just 47% in the space of two deliveries.

slides.headline: Suryakumar out — India's win chance hits its low
slides.body: Suryakumar Yada, one of India's favourite hitters, was caught behind by Klaasen off Rabada. The batting side's win chance slid down to 38% — the lowest point of the innings so far.

slides.headline: Kohli & Dube steadying the ship — can India push past 140?
slides.body: Kohli (46 off 43) and Dube (9 off 5) have shared 12 runs off just 9 balls to calm the innings. Watch whether Kohli can keep scoring and push the total past 140+ before the next wave of wickets falls.

slides.headline: Maharaj snags Pant's wicket at 1.6 to swing the game
slides.body: In the first over, Keshav Maharaj caught Gautam Pandey (Pant) out at 1.6, a key moment that dropped the team's win chances from 56% to 47%. It was an early shock that set the tone for the innings.

slides.headline: Unusually high-scoring 19th over by Jansen
slides.body: The 19th over (18.1-18.6) saw 17 runs off Marco Jansen, a huge 2.25 standard deviations above average. This burst kept India’s target high and made the chase harder for South Africa.

slides.headline: Suryakumar's wicket at 4.3 turns momentum
slides.body: At 4.3, Kagiso Rabada caught Suryakumar to reduce India’s chance to 38%. A quick wicket that was a surprise swing and showed how the bowlers were threatening.

slides.headline: What to watch as South Africa chase 177
slides.body: South Africa now face 177 runs from 120 balls with a 8.85 run‑rate requirement. Look for bowlers trying to bowl tight, and the batting side looking for quick runs. Every wicket will shift the balance.

slides.headline: Explosive start: 15 runs in the first over
slides.body: India began with a bang, scoring 15 runs in the very first over bowled by Marco Jansen. That's well above the norm, putting early pressure on South Africa.

slides.headline: Two early wickets swing momentum
slides.body: Maharaj struck twice in his second over, dismissing Rohit (caught by Klaasen) and Pant (caught by de Kock). Those wickets cut India's win chance from 65% to 47%.

slides.headline: A rare 7‑ball dot spell
slides.body: From ball 1.3 to 2.3, India went seven consecutive deliveries without a run, the longest scoreless stretch so far, showing South Africa’s bowling bite.

slides.headline: What to watch: steady partnership and run rate
slides.body: India are 45 for 3 after six overs, scoring at 7.5 runs per over. The key now is a solid partnership (Kohli and Axar) to keep the run rate up while protecting wickets. Win chance sits at 42%.

slides.headline: Over 15: 24 runs in a single over – a 3σ outlier
slides.body: Axar Patel’s sixth over produced 24 runs (6,4,6,4,2,2). That’s three standard deviations above the typical 6‑run over, spiking South Africa’s score from 123 to 147 and lifting win probability to 87%.

slides.headline: 12.3 – de Kock dismissed, win chance dips 14%
slides.body: Arshdeep Singh trapped David de Kock LBW (caught by Kuldeep). South Africa’s win odds fell from 43% to 29%, showing the wicket’s impact despite a high run rate.

slides.headline: Miller‑Klaasen partnership fuels chase
slides.body: David Miller (14 off 7) and Heinrich Klaasen (49 off 22) added 41 runs in 15 balls, raising the run rate to 9.8. Their aggressive combo shifted the chase momentum and set a comfortable platform for the final 30 runs.

slides.headline: What to watch: 30 runs needed off 30 balls
slides.body: South Africa need 30 runs from 30 balls (RR 6). Keep an eye on Klaasen vs Arshdeep (right‑hand powerplay) and Miller vs Jasprit Bumrah. Any wicket will raise pressure; a single over of 12+ runs will seal the win.

slides.headline: De Kock out, SA's win chance dips
slides.body: Arshdeep Singh bowled De Kock for a duck at 12.3, dropping South Africa’s win probability from 43% to 29%. SA are now 147/4, needing 30 runs from 30 balls.

slides.headline: Axar Patel's over 15 fires 24 runs
slides.body: Axar Patel’s over 15 produced 24 runs – three standard deviations above the norm – turning the match. A six at 14.3 lifted SA’s win chance to 67%. Six balls, 24 runs, a huge boost.

slides.headline: Rare three‑ball dot spell in over 9
slides.body: A three‑ball dot spell (no run) ran from 9.1 to 9.3, an uncommon tight spell. It showed India’s bowlers could bite, even as SA kept a high scoring rate overall.

slides.headline: What to watch: 30 runs needed in 30 balls
slides.body: South Africa need 30 runs off the last 30 balls (required run rate 6). Keep the wickets, let Miller and Klaasen continue the partnership, and watch for big hits or a tight Indian spell that could swing the finish.

slides.headline: Axar’s Six Shocks the Match – South Africa’s Win Chance Soars
slides.body: In the 14.3rd ball of the 15th over, Axar Patel hit a six to Klaasen, pushing South Africa’s chance to win from 55 % to 67 %. Think of it like a striker scoring a penalty in the 70th minute that swings the game in their favor.

slides.headline: Early Wicket Slumps the Momentum – Win Chance Drops to 29 %
slides.body: The 12.3rd ball of the 13th over, Arshdeep Singh’s delivery to de Kock was caught by Kuldeep Yadav, cutting the win probability from 43 % to 29 %. It’s akin to a team losing a key defender early, putting pressure on the rest of the squad.

slides.headline: Over 15 Delivers a Record 24 Runs – A Cricketing Flurry
slides.body: Axar Patel’s over 15 produced 24 runs, a 3.08‑σ above average. In football terms, it’s like one player scoring four goals in a single quarter, instantly changing the scoreline.

slides.headline: Three Overs, 22 Runs – The Pressure Builds
slides.body: South Africa now needs 22 runs from 18 balls with a required run rate of 7.33, compared to a current run rate of 9.12. Imagine a team needing 22 points in the final 3 overs – the urgency is high. Stay tuned for how they tackle this chase.

slides.headline: Bumrah’s wicket at 17.4 shifts the battle
slides.body: At 17.4, Jasprit Bumrah bowled South Africa’s top‑order batsman, reducing South Africa’s win chance from 73 % to 55 % and tightening the chase.

slides.headline: Axar Patel’s 24‑run over stuns India
slides.body: Over 15, Axar Patel hit a record 24 runs in 6 balls. It’s a huge surprise for India and a big boost for South Africa, who are now 20 runs short with 12 balls left.

slides.headline: What to watch next: 12 balls and 20 runs to go
slides.body: Only 12 balls left and 20 runs are needed. That’s 10 runs per over. South Africa will need big hits and good bowling to keep the chase alive. Watch for the next 6‑ball over.

slides.headline: Key wicket drops SA's win odds
slides.body: Bumrah bowled Hendricks out at 1.3 (event 1415755:0145). That wicket cut South Africa’s win probability from 33% to just 21%, a big swing in the early innings.

slides.headline: Very quiet start with two dot balls
slides.body: The match began with a very quiet spell – the first two balls (0.1‑0.2, events 1415755:0137 & 1415755:0138) produced no runs, the longest scoreless stretch so far.

slides.headline: Four to Hendricks gives a tiny win‑chance boost
slides.body: Arshdeep hit a four to Hendricks at 0.6 (event 1415755:0142), nudging SA’s win chance up from 30% to 33% – a brief lift amid the early wickets.

slides.headline: What to watch from now on
slides.body: South Africa sit at 42/2 after six overs, needing 135 runs from 84 balls (9.64 runs per over). Keep an eye on the Stubbs‑de Kock partnership and whether they can speed up before the next wicket falls.

slides.headline: Hardik’s wicket pulls South Africa’s win chance down
slides.body: At 16.1, Hardik to Klaasen, caught by Pant. Wickets fell, South Africa’s win chance dropped from 88% to 78%. Overs left 16.1-18.0, 12 balls, 20 runs needed.

slides.headline: 17.4 Bumrah to Jansen, OUT, bowled
slides.body: Bumrah’s fourth ball in over 17 bowls Jansen, reducing win chance 73% to 55%. Runs still 20 required, but pressure mounts.

slides.headline: 12 balls left, 20 runs to score
slides.body: South Africa trailing by 20, 12 balls remaining. Required run rate 10, current run rate 8.72. Need to maintain 1.3x run rate. Bowlers must limit boundaries.

slides.headline: Miller vs Jansen: crucial 12 balls
slides.body: South Africa needs 20 runs from 12 balls, 1 wicket in hand. Focus on David Miller’s ability to score quick boundaries and on Jansen’s line and length to contain. Target 10.8 RPS for batting, 8.0 RPS to bowl.
